name: DRAWN FROM LIFE · twelve small films for the season
one_line: Twelve small hand-drawn films of the private moments of an Indian woman's festive and wedding season, in violet ink and peach, sage and lilac watercolour on warm paper, where everything is drawn except the jewellery: in every film one drawn everyday thing turns into the photographed piece, and when the drawing fades away, the piece stays.
big_idea: THE IDEA IN THREE SECONDS: a drawing of an Indian moment, and the only thing in it that isn't drawn is the jewellery. DRAWN FROM LIFE is a season of twelve tiny illustrated films (eight Reels on weekdays, four flipbook carousels on Sundays) about the small private moments of a festive and wedding season, seen without faces: a Sunday plait, a terrace waiting for the moon, a steel tiffin of gifts, the aukshan thali, the Dhanteras polishing, a rangoli, a box she wrapped for herself, the first wedding card, the tailor's mirror, wet mehendi, safety pins in the pleats, and the heavy jhumkas coming off at 2 a.m. Every film is drawn by one invisible steel nib in violet ink (cream chalk on the night papers) with flat watercolour washes from the brand deck's peach tulips and sage leaves, and every film obeys the same four-beat grammar, so the twelve read as one series: (1) THE MOMENT DRAWS ITSELF on warm paper; (2) THE RHYME: one drawn everyday shape becomes the photographed piece in exactly its place (the plait becomes the Woven Gold Hoop's braid, the aarti lamp's circle becomes the Ruby bracelet, the rangoli's line becomes the Prism Rivière, the mehendi's dots-to-a-drop become the Mint Pear Drops); this is the account's best ad ever, 'Anaar, pre-peeled.' (ROAS 4.52), turned into a motion device; (3) THE LINE: one Velista headline and one lowercase Cormorant turn, one witty, true, Indian idea per film; (4) THE PIECE STAYS: the drawing un-draws itself stroke by stroke until only the jewellery is left on the empty page, above a gallery-style label with its name, finish, one exact fact and live price. The series sign-off, on every end card, is the brand's whole argument in seven words: the moment goes. the piece stays. It is the owner's 'Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.' told as a story, and the season ends on it literally: N° 12, top-left of the grid, the heavy wedding jhumkas come off at 2 a.m. and the ruby huggies stay. Three honesty rules are also the look: the pen never touches the piece (a 14 px halo of bare paper around every photograph); on a body the drawing is built at the piece's listed size (a 25 mm hoop against a drawn ear), and on objects any enlargement is labelled 'shown larger.'; everything drawn is declared drawn, so nothing pretends to be a photograph. The grid is the thirteenth drawing: every cover is finished like a signed, numbered print (edition number left, the punchline as a pencil-italic inscription in the middle, the NAIRA wordmark as the artist's signature right); day films sit on pale blush, sage and lilac papers and night films on violet, oxblood and bottle-green toned papers, so the twelve covers continue the LAC / flower / BONE checkerboard straight up the profile with a violet spine down the centre column; one horizon line at the same height runs across every row like a storyboard; and the columns are weekdays (Tuesday films right, Friday films centre, Sunday flipbooks left). Sound has a signature too: every film opens on the scratch of a nib and lands the piece on one small 'ting'.
why_better_than_A_and_B: Measured against the two options the judges are choosing from (Matching Centre, the likely A; MANGAL or the Reissue, the likely B): (1) MOTION-NATIVE. All twelve posts move: eight films and four flipbooks whose every slide loops. A and B are 8 to 10 stills plus two or three reels assembled from stills; Instagram now treats every feed video as a Reel and pushes it to non-followers, which a relaunch after 76 silent days needs. (2) THE PROVEN MECHANISM BECOMES THE MOTION. The one creative idea with hard numbers in this account is the everyday-Indian rhyme where the piece is the punchline ('Anaar, pre-peeled.' ₹335 per purchase, ROAS 4.52; concept 1.44x vs plain 0.57x). V3 does it on screen in every film: the drawn thing visibly becomes the piece. A carries a shade tag and B a seal; neither makes the product the payoff of every post. (3) OWNER'S TASTE, NOT JUST THE REFERENCE'S. The judges flagged MANGAL at about nine layers per tile, its nine-script key art and marigold ground, and Matching Centre's wandering tag and AI textiles. V3 has no stickers, stamps, seals, sunbursts, price labels or swatch soup: each cover is one drawing, one photographed piece, one headline and one signed margin; two Devanagari words in the whole season (आई, शुभ विवाह) instead of ten languages; no black, sand or beige ground; slow, calm, owner-paced motion (one nib, one camera move, no cuts). (4) HONEST BY CONSTRUCTION. Drawn means drawn and only the jewellery is a photograph; true scale on bodies; 'shown larger.' on objects; listing words only ('18k gold tone plated', 'rhodium coated', 'green cubic zirconia', never 'emerald' or 'gold'); not one water claim anywhere. (5) BUILDABLE WITHOUT THE AMATEUR RISK. The judges' biggest production flag was agents drawing anatomy. V3's figures (hands, napes, ears, a silhouette) come from 12 AI line plates in one house hand, revealed by traced mask paths; everything geometric (tiffin, thali, rangoli, card, box, shelf, pins, jhumka) is agent SVG through one shared ink filter; one film template, one label, one set-down, one glint. (6) THE GRID IS DESIGNED AS A PICTURE. A value checkerboard that climbs straight out of LAC / flower / BONE, mirror-symmetric jewel nights (oxblood at r1c1 and r3c3, bottle green at r1c3 and r3c1, violet down the centre), weekday columns, one horizon line per row, and a signed margin under every tile. A is a shade card, B a poster wall; V3 is a sketchbook you can read from across the room. (7) A THESIS THAT SELLS THE CATEGORY'S JOB. 'The moment goes. The piece stays.' frames demi-fine as what you keep wearing after the festival, ending on the 2 a.m. finale with the Ruby set as the BUY3 basket. (8) BUILT FROM WHAT ONCE BROKE THE ACCOUNT OUT: sketching ('masterji sketching dreams', 3,149 likes) and unboxing ('The Naira Experience', 3,410), 100 to 300 times the 9.5-like median. It also absorbs the judges' best graftable ideas in its own form: a forwardable Bhaubeej hint, a tailor's-question neckline guide, a self-gift Padwa, a steel-tiffin gift guide and a top-left Ruby closer.
why_it_fits: BRAND. It turns up what Naira already owns rather than borrowing PTAT's look: the brand deck's watercolour peach tulips and sage leaves become the washes; the Lilac edition mast #4E3C66 (the colour the owner asked for) becomes the ink; the camp and exhibition grounds become the night papers; Velista caps plus a lowercase Cormorant italic turn plus Jost labels stay the only type system; the wordmark appears once per frame, as a signature; radius 0; 'Softly, slowly, worn.' and the box band's 'Crafted for the moments you keep.' are the series' own spirit; the house devices (N° numbering, bracketed material kickers, honest 'X, not Y' corrections) carry through. It is Hermès-grade line and Wes Anderson framing (centred, symmetrical, folio captions, a signed title card) in Naira's palette, with Indian life as the subject and never as wallpaper (one Indian object per frame, material and domestic rather than iconographic, no deity, no firecracker). OWNER TASTE. Loves: Indian everyday-object wit with restraint, lilac and purple, deck florals as washes not stickers, chic minimal still life with one meaningful object, moody night grounds (oxblood, emerald-green, plum), exact facts, slow motion she tunes herself. Avoids everything she has sent back: clutter, stuck-on florals, black or sand grounds, cool light, brassy gold, grand copy, discount art, full faces, lyrics on reels, food props, anything that reads AI-made (the drawings are declared drawings; the jewellery is the listing photograph). DATA. Buyer: women 35 and over are 64% of purchases (35 to 54 alone, 54%); Maharashtra 46% of orders (aukshan, faral, Padwa, rangoli and the tailor's 'gala' are hers). Products: the five bestsellers (Woven Gold Hoops 20 units, Prism Rivière top revenue ₹27,649, Ruby Baguette Tennis Bracelet 13 since 16 Oct with Ruby 8 of 13, Heartbead 11, Brushed Gold Huggies 8) each get a tile, and the deepest unsold stock gets the rest (Baguette Tennis Necklace 70 in stock and 0 sold, Bold Nocturne Chain 53/2, Kiss Knot Bangle 40/0, North Star Bangle 20/0, Mint Pear Drops 20/0, Duo Link Bracelet 20/0); 8 of 12 posts are Edition Two, the account's best week ever (34 purchases at ₹854). Timing: the gift guide lands a week before Diwali, the Bhaubeej hint eight days early, Karwa Chauth on the evening itself; Sunday noon (about 27% of orders) carries the four shoppable flipbooks. Feed and Stories stills earned 84% of attributed purchases, so the flipbooks keep a still label slide and every film ends on a price card; paid Reels sold poorly (ROAS 0.49), so the films are built for organic reach and sends (hint, tag-the-cousin, RSVP), not as ads.
motion_language: House rules of movement for DRAWN FROM LIFE (owner-paced: calm, continuous, nothing jittery). 1 ONE PEN, ONE PACE. Every line is drawn by one invisible steel nib at a constant 520 px/s for contours and 700 px/s for small details (linear within a stroke, 60 to 120 ms pen-lift between strokes); a film's drawing takes 4 to 6 s. Lines are never faded in: they are drawn or un-drawn. 2 THE PAGE NEVER HURRIES. At most one camera move per film, a slow push or drift (scale ≤ 1.0→2.4 only in P1's single push to the ear; elsewhere ≤ 1.0→1.06, or translate ≤ 120 px) on cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1) over ≥ 4 s; parallax only between paper/wash (0.6x) and line/piece (1x). No cuts inside a film; any change of view is a cross-dissolve ≥ 600 ms or a match-dissolve. 3 COLOUR ARRIVES AS WATER. Washes bloom from a point (usually the piece) through an expanding circle mask (CSS r on an SVG <circle>) whose edge is roughened by filter #wet (feTurbulence baseFrequency .012, numOctaves 2 + feDisplacementMap scale 38), 1.8 to 2.4 s on cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); they drain back the same way in 1.2 s. 4 THE PIECE IS SET DOWN, NEVER FLOWN IN: opacity 0→1, blur 6→0 px, scale 1.035→1, translateY −14→0 px, drop-shadow from (0 34px 40px rgba(40,22,10,.08)) to (0 16px 18px rgba(40,22,10,.22)) plus (0 3px 4px rgba(40,22,10,.18)), 900 ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). It never spins, bounces, wobbles or zooms; maximum rotation 2° except where a film rotates it once into its resting angle. 5 THE RHYME IS A MATCH-DISSOLVE: the drawn shape holds 300 ms, its stroke retracts from both ends (700 ms) while the photograph develops in exactly its footprint; the two overlap ≥ 400 ms so the eye reads one becoming the other. 6 ONE GLINT PER FILM: the site's four-point sparkle (path M6 0L7.5 4.5L12 6L7.5 7.5L6 12L4.5 7.5L0 6L4.5 4.5Z) at 54 px, white with a 6 px blur glow, scale .6→1.1→0 and rotate 0→45° over 700 ms on the brightest stone or crest; plus one light sweep, a 120 px white linear-gradient band at 18°, mix-blend-mode screen, opacity .55, masked to the cut-out's alpha, crossing the piece in 1.1 s cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1). The audio 'ting' lands on the glint. 7 TYPE arrives like the website's reveal: 16 px rise + fade, 600 ms, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), 120 ms between lines; the Cormorant italic turn is written on by a soft left-to-right mask wipe (900 ms, cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1)) 500 ms after the headline. No kinetic type, no scaling, no type over the piece, no lyrics, no captions timed to music. 8 THE PAPER HALO: no line comes within 14 px of the piece; the halo is a static mask made from the cut-out's alpha dilated by 14 px (feMorphology dilate radius 14), subtracted from the line layer only. 9 THE PIECE STAYS (exit): the headline fades 400 ms; every line un-draws in reverse drawing order at 1.6x speed; washes drain toward the piece; the horizon line stays; the piece alone glides to the label position (1.2 s, cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1), scale ≤ 1.25, rotation settles to 0). 10 THE LABEL builds in 120 ms steps and holds ≥ 2.2 s. 11 LOOPS: frame 0 of every film is the empty paper with only the horizon line; the last 500 ms fade the label and piece back to exactly that state, so Instagram's auto-loop is seamless. Flipbook slide 1 is a cover-first loop: its first and last frames are the designed cover, so the grid thumbnail is always the cover. 12 NIGHT LIGHT: on night papers lines are cream; lamps are soft radial glows of --expo-gold at 22 to 35% that 'breathe' 0.85→1 over 3.2 s (never faster than 1.6 s a cycle, never a flicker). 13 WHAT NEVER MOVES: the horizon line, the wordmark (it only fades), the paper and grain, type once landed, and the piece once set down (except its one exit glide). Never: shake, zoom-blur, flash, wipe transitions, glitch, speed ramps, confetti, sparkle storms, petals. 14 RENDERING (tools/reel.cjs seeks document.getAnimations() frame by frame at 30 fps): all motion is CSS @keyframes / Web Animations on HTML and inline SVG (stroke-dashoffset with pathLength=1, mask, clip-path, transform incl. 3D with perspective, opacity, filter, CSS r, CSS d for the P7 ribbon); SMIL is not used. Anything CSS cannot animate (feTurbulence seed drift for wet edges, feDisplacementMap scale) is set per frame in window.atTime(ms). Reels render at 1080x1920; flipbook video slides need the same script with a 1080x1440 viewport. AI line plates (black on transparent) are recoloured by using them as mask-image on an ink-coloured layer and revealed through hand-authored mask paths (centre-line strokes traced along the drawing in drawing order, stroke-width 36 px, round caps, stroke-dashoffset 1→0). Agent-drawn SVG shares filter #ink (feTurbulence baseFrequency .02, numOctaves 2, a different seed per object; feDisplacementMap scale 2.2) and 3.2 px main / 2 px detail widths, so geometric objects carry the same hand as the plates; check side by side at 100% before render.

grid_system.type_system: Three faces only, as shipped. DISPLAY: Velista 400, caps only (it is unicase), for every cover and in-film headline at 84 to 120 px (≥ 84 px so it reads at 30 to 43 px in the 391x521 grid tile), line-height .95, tracking .01em, max 3 lines, always ending in a full stop or question mark; also piece names on end cards (56 px; Velista carries È, so PRISM RIVIÈRE stays in Velista). Velista has no ₹ and no middle dot: prices are Jost with the ₹ falling back to Poppins (--nf-font-label), and every '·' is set in Jost. EDITORIAL TURN: Cormorant Garamond italic 400, lowercase, 52 to 56 px in-film under the headline, 36 px as the signed-margin inscription on covers, 40 px for the sign-off 'the moment goes. the piece stays.', 30 to 40 px for anything written inside the drawing (the gift tag, the chit, tier engravings): the series uses Cormorant as its 'fair hand', never a handwriting font (no Kalam). LABELS: Jost 500 caps 22 to 26 px tracking .24em for edition numbers and eyebrows (one per frame), Jost 300 24 to 28 px for folios and bracket lines, Jost 400 44 px for prices. DEVANAGARI: Tiro Devanagari Marathi for exactly two in-world words, आई (P3 tier engraving) and शुभ विवाह (P8 card head), both checked by a native reader before render. Type never sits over the piece or its 14 px halo, never animates beyond a 16 px rise or a left-to-right ink wipe, and never sits in the top-right 16% x 14% of a cover.
grid_system.emblem: THE SIGNED MARGIN (on every one of the 12 covers, identical in position). Every cover is finished like a signed, numbered print: under the horizon line, in the paper margin, at baseline tile y 1338 (reel cover y 1578): LEFT the edition number 'N° 07/12' (Jost 500 26 px, tracking .24em, ink colour); CENTRE the film's punchline as a pencil-style inscription in Cormorant Garamond italic 36 px lowercase (e.g. 'the huggies stay.'), the second beat of the Velista headline above it; RIGHT the NAIRA wordmark as the artist's signature (kit/naira-wordmark.svg inlined and recoloured: violet #4E3C66 letters + blush #FFBDA8 flower on day papers, cream #F6EFE6 + blush on night papers; 176 px wide, right edge x 1008; never redrawn, never twice in a frame). In the grid the twelve margins line up row by row like a wall of framed prints, and '/12' tells a visitor there is a set to collect. In motion the emblem is the piece alone on the empty page inside its 14 px paper halo: the last image of every film. On reel covers the 240 px above and below the tile carry only paper and the continuation of the wash and drawing (no type, no piece), so the full 9:16 cover in the Reels tab reads as the same drawing with more air.
grid_system.lockup: END-CARD LABEL (identical in all eight films and as the last still of each flipbook, 'the gallery label'): on the film's own paper, the piece alone, centred at x 540, y about 690 (reels; flipbook stills y about 520), at 1.1 to 1.25x its film size with its contact shadow; then a text block left-aligned at x 96, inside the reel-safe area (y 270 to 1250, and x ≤ 860 below y 1150 to clear the right-hand action rail): y 930 Cormorant italic 40 px 'the moment goes. the piece stays.'; y 1004 Jost 500 22 px tracking .24em 'N° 04 · DRAWN FROM LIFE'; y 1040 the piece name in Velista 56 px (two lines at 52 px if longer than 15 characters); y 1112 Jost 300 28 px the bracket line '[ finish · one exact listing fact ]'; y 1160 the live price in Jost 400 44 px plus 'nairaflore.com' Jost 300 28 px tracking .08em at x 300; y 1208 the wordmark at 200 px wide. Builds in 120 ms steps (16 px rise, 600 ms, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)) and holds at least 2.2 s. SERIES TITLE LOCKUP (P1 cover, P12 slide 5): Velista 'DRAWN FROM LIFE.' over Cormorant italic 'twelve small films.'
grid_system.recurring_devices: 1 THE RHYME: in every film one drawn everyday thing becomes the photographed piece by match-dissolve in exactly its place (plait→braided hoop; stars→engraved stars; lamp circle→ruby bracelet; polishing→the one already polished; rangoli line→Prism; ribbon knot→the bangle's X; the card's linked rings→linked links; the tailor's tape→the baguette line; mehendi dots-to-drop→three pears to one mint pear; two-metal safety pins→two-tone links; heavy jhumka off→huggie stays). 2 THE PEN NEVER TOUCHES THE PIECE: a 14 px halo of bare paper around every photograph. 3 THE PIECE STAYS: every film exits by un-drawing in reverse until only the jewellery remains, then the label; sign-off 'the moment goes. the piece stays.' 4 THE HORIZON LINE: a 4 px ink line at tile y 1150 (cover y 1390), edge to edge on every cover (a parapet, a shelf, a table, a threshold, a floor), so each grid row carries one continuous line like a storyboard strip; it is already drawn at frame 0 and never moves. 5 THE SIGNED MARGIN (see emblem). 6 TRUE SCALE: on a body the drawing is built around the piece's listed size; on an object, any enlargement says 'shown larger.' in Jost 20 px. 7 THE FOLIO: each film opens with a time-of-day and place in Jost caps at top-left ('NIGHT · THE TERRACE'), never a clock time or date. 8 THE NIB AND THE TING: the scratch of a steel nib under every drawing and one small bell-like 'ting' when the piece arrives: the series' sound logo. 9 DAY AND NIGHT PAPERS alternating as a checkerboard. 10 WEEKDAY COLUMNS: Tuesday films (column 3), Thursday/Friday films (column 2), Sunday flipbooks (column 1). 11 CROSS-REFERENCES: films point to each other where pieces form sets (N° 05 chain ↔ N° 08 drops; N° 09 Duo Link Necklace ↔ N° 11 Duo Link Bracelet; N° 04 Ruby bracelet ↔ N° 12 Ruby set). 12 THE FLOWER CAMEO (optional, owner's call): the I-flower from the wordmark hides once in each drawing as part of an object, 40 to 60 px, in the line colour (the oil bottle's label, a rangoli centre, a mehendi rosette, the thali rim); it rewards rewatching and gives the first comment a game; delete it and nothing else changes.

grid_system.transition_to_existing_grid: Row 4 sits directly on the live August row (LAC | flower | BONE): P3 sage-day over LAC's oxblood, P2 violet-night over the cream flower tile, P1 blush-day over BONE's oxblood: dark over light and light over dark, so the checkerboard climbs straight up out of the old row instead of starting again. The old row's big serif-on-colour words rhyme with the new Velista headlines in the same top-left corner; P2 is a negative of the flower tile (a violet night with small stars directly above a cream page with one dark flower); LAC's oxblood is absorbed into the new system twice (P4 r3c3 and P12 r1c1) rather than left as an orphan; nothing repeats LAC or BONE's words. The rows below (Aug stills of single pieces on oxblood and plaster) keep reading as the archive the series grew out of. If any post goes up late, Instagram's grid reordering (rolled out 8 Jun 2026) restores the slot.
grid_system.pins: 0 pins during the run. Pinning moves a post out of its slot and would break the checkerboard, the weekday columns and the row horizons; the composition is designed to be read unpinned. After 22 Nov, if the owner wants a pin, pin nothing from this set and use a future post, or pin three at once so the shift is a whole row.

posts.concept: Every woman this feed is for knows the Sunday oiling and the plait done so tight her eyebrows lifted; half of them now do it for a daughter. The pen draws the back of a head from behind, a drop of oil, a comb, three strands, and an older woman's two hands weaving them down the nape. The camera eases in to the ear, where a drawn hoop outline waits at the lobe; the plait's over-under braid dissolves into the photographed Woven Gold Hoop, a braided rope of gold-tone strands about 25 mm across. MUMMY'S PLAIT. in gold tone. The bestseller is explained by the most familiar braid in India, and N° 01 teaches the season's whole grammar: everything is drawn except the piece; one drawn thing becomes the piece; the drawing goes, the piece stays. Its cover is the season's key art (DRAWN FROM LIFE over the plait and the hoop), and the caption owns the 76-day silence with one honest wink: we were drawing.

posts.caption:
We went quiet for eleven weeks. We were drawing.

Mummy's Sunday plait, tight enough to lift your eyebrows, drawn from life. The Woven Gold Hoops are braided the same way: a thick rope of gold-tone strands, about 25 mm across, no stones. Our bestseller, ₹1,299.

This is N° 01 of DRAWN FROM LIFE, twelve small films for the festive and wedding season. Everything in them is drawn, except the jewellery. New films on Tuesdays and Fridays, a flipbook on Sundays.

posts.concept: Karwa Chauth's one universal joke is that the moon is always late: on every terrace in north India someone refreshes the moonrise time and stares at the clouds. The film is the wait, from behind: a silhouette at a terrace wall at night, dupatta over her head, a chalni (sieve) held up to an empty sky. The pen draws a cloud over the moon's spot, then, when it is nearly clear, a second one (a small comic beat). Meanwhile the stars arrive, one by one, eight-pointed, on time. Three of them drift down to her raised wrist and become the photographed North Star Bangle, whose face alternates engraved eight-point stars with round clear stones. THE MOON IS LATE. the stars came on time. Only then does half a moon appear. Posted at 7 p.m. on the day, so it lands on phones on the terrace, mid-wait. No husband, no fasting talk, no gift pressure: it is about her and the sky.

posts.caption:
The heavy ones come off at 2 a.m. The huggies stay.

After the first wedding of the season, the jhumkas go back in their box and the box goes back to the locker. The Baguette Huggies don't go anywhere: about 18 mm, one row of baguettes standing crosswise along the lower front, the upper half plain polished gold tone, a hinged snap. In ruby-red, clear, green or purple cubic zirconia. ₹1,199.

Swipe for the whole ruby set, huggies, bracelet and the 36 cm necklace: ₹5,198 for all three. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off, with codes BUY2 and BUY3 at checkout.

That is the last of our twelve films for the season. Thank you for watching them.

risks: Build load: 8 Reels (14 to 18 s) and 4 flipbooks (5 to 6 slides, 3 to 5 of them looping) is about 30 motion clips. Mitigation: one shared film template (paper, halo, set-down, glint, un-draw, label, inscription as components), 18 AI plates in one style block, geometric SVG for all objects; build P1 first as the template and review it with the owner before the other 11.

AI line plates of hands can come out with wrong fingers or a 'generated' smoothness. Mitigation: line art is easy to inspect; budget allows one retry per plate (18 used of 25); reject anything with a face, a stray ornament or jewellery; if a plate still reads AI-made, simplify it to an agent-drawn single-line gesture.

Style mismatch between AI plates and agent SVG (perfect geometry beside a pen line). Mitigation: shared #ink displacement filter and matched stroke widths (3.2 / 2 px), checked side by side at 100% before rendering.

Ruby stock is thin (bracelet Ruby 12, huggies Ruby 12, selling about one a day) and Ruby leads P4 and P12. Swap rules are written into each post (P4 → Ruby necklace, 20; P12 → Amethyst huggies and the Crystal or Emerald set); re-read roster.json each posting morning.

Paid data says Reels sold poorly (ROAS 0.49 vs Feed 1.15). The films are for organic reach and sends; the four Sunday flipbooks carry the shoppable detail and are the ones to boost if any post is boosted.
